paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, ainsi donc, les négociations d’adhésion s’ouvrent enfin avec la Moldavie: il était temps! Le peuple moldave l’a dit, redit et le répète encore: il se sent européen, il veut entrer dans l’Union européenne. Il a voté en ce sens à plusieurs reprises, en dépit des pressions insensées que la Russie a fait peser sur lui. Manipulation de l’information, achats de voix, oligarques à la botte de Moscou, gangs criminels, pressions économiques: la petite Moldavie a eu droit à tout et a résisté à tout.

On la regarde parfois avec condescendance: on ferait mieux d’en prendre de la graine. Parce que des manipulations de l’information, des groupes de médias étrangers bienveillants vis-à-vis de Vladimir Poutine et des tentatives d’intimidation, eh bien ça ne se passe pas qu’en Moldavie.

Le peuple moldave veut rejoindre l’Union européenne, et ses autorités savent ce qu’elles ont à faire, les réformes qu’elles ont à mener pour y parvenir. Mais nous, est-ce que nous savons ce que nous voulons? Sommes-nous prêts à accueillir de nouveaux membres dans notre Union? J’ai bien peur que nous n’ayons pas encore pris la mesure du monde qui nous entoure.
L’élargissement de l’Union européenne peut être une chance: celle d’échapper à notre encerclement. Mais sa réussite va dépendre aussi de nous.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, Russia's brutal war of aggression has shown that there are no grey zones on our continent, no place for grey zones. We must therefore continue supporting all enlargement countries who are demonstrating willingness to progress on the path of EU integration.
Moldova has shown a strong determination in the implementation of reforms, in the face of challenging circumstances, despite disinformation campaigns and hybrid attacks from Russia.
While there are still some changes necessary, of course, we cannot allow Moscow to undermine Moldova's European cause.

Russia's actions remind us that enlargement is not a bureaucratic exercise, but one of the EU's most important geopolitical instruments to strengthen stability, security and prosperity across our continent.
Candidate countries must deliver on reforms. At the same time, the EU has to remain a reliable partner.

paragraphs.text: Doamnă comisar, domnule președinte, stimați colegi, programul ambițios al Republicii Moldova pentru a încheia aderarea la sfârșitul anului 2028 trebuie susținut. Este de salutat, dar nu va putea fi pus în aplicare dacă nu îl susținem toți. Și vreau de la bun început să mulțumesc și doamnei comisar, și colegilor care au susținut acest proiect.

Sunt româncă, sunt moldoveancă, cunosc foarte bine Republica Moldova, cunosc cetățenii de acolo, cetățenii își doresc acest lucru și trebuie să-i încurajăm pentru a avea încredere în proiectul Uniunii Europene, pentru că are nevoie administrația de la Chișinău de susținerea populară.

Sigur că nu văd alt drum și trebuie să fim și realiști: Republica Moldova e la graniță, cât de greu este să reziste la atacurile directe, indirecte, fake news-urile și tot ce se întâmplă acolo cu Rusia. Uniunea Europeană este un proiect la care eu, ca româncă, mi-am dorit să fim cu țara mea acolo. De aceea, doamna comisar, Consiliul, Parlamentul trebuie să înțeleagă că Republica Moldova are locul ei în Uniunea Europeană și trebuie să o susținem.

Și mai vreau să adaug un lucru: cred foarte tare că ceea ce acum se întâmplă în Ucraina ține în loc și Republica Moldova. Trebuie să separăm. România și Bulgaria a pățit același lucru cu Schengen. Haideți să fim corecți, obiectivi - în Ucraina nu se pot respecta termenele și jaloanele - și să dăm drumul Moldovei și, la terminarea anului 2028, Republica Moldova să fie în marea familie.

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, stimați colegi, mă bucur că Republica Moldova a deschis primul capitol de negociere pentru aderarea la Uniunea Europeană. De acum, datoria noastră este să nu transformăm acest drum european într-o sală de așteptare fără sfârșit. Republica Moldova trebuie evaluată corect. Este firesc ca România să susțină Republica Moldova în parcursul său de aderare la Uniunea Europeană.

Sprijinirea românilor de peste Prut este o datorie istorică și o necesitate strategică. Cu atât mai mult cu cât aproape jumătate din ei sunt și cetățeni ai României. Integrarea sa în Uniunea Europeană reprezintă mai multă stabilitate și mai multă siguranță la frontiera estică a Uniunii. Însă Republica Moldova trebuie să continue să se desprindă de moștenirea sa sovietică, precum și de reflexele trecutului, iar Bruxelles-ul trebuie să-și dovedească deschiderea pentru un rezultat final concret și neîntârziat.

Dacă românii de peste ambele maluri ale Prutului nu s-au putut reunifica precum berlinezii, atunci Republica Moldova și România trebuie să se reunifice măcar prin apartenența lor la Uniunea Europeană.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, thank you for the excellent report, Sven Mikser. I cannot stress enough the importance of opening all negotiation clusters for Moldova and Ukraine. Article 49 of the Treaty of European Union clearly states that unanimity is required only for the opening and closing of accession negotiations. But what is the European Council doing? The endless unanimity silos for each chapter are like sand that the Council is throwing in the gears of enlargement.

The situation now is that the Member States are undermining European security, delaying the enlargement process, sabotaging our strategic interests and preventing effective, comprehensive negotiations on all clusters with Moldova. Let us do our best to fulfil our promise to start closing all chapters at the beginning of 2027, as promised.

Dear friends in Moldova and Ukraine, please continue your reforms with the same spirit as before. Please trust us, and we will do our utmost to have you sitting in this Parliament among us in the nearest future. Let's do it!

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, doamnă comisar, doamnelor și domnilor, astăzi nu decidem doar asupra parcursului european al Republicii Moldova. Decidem și cât de credibilă este Uniunea Europeană atunci când un popor își asumă valorile noastre și are curajul să le apere.

Republica Moldova nu cere favoruri. Vine cu reforme, cu sacrificii și cu alegere democratică reafirmate de cetățenii săi. Vine cu demnitate și cu rezistența remarcabilă în fața presiunii și amenințării ruse. De aceea, Republica Moldova nu este doar un stat candidat. Este dovada că proiectul european inspiră, mobilizează și oferă speranțe. Pentru România acest sprijin este o responsabilitate istorică. Pentru Uniunea Europeană, este o chestiune de credibilitate.

Nu putem cere curaj celor care aleg Europa și apoi să-i părăsim. Reformele trebuie să continue în Moldova, iar noi trebuie să răspundem cu un sprijin ferm și consecvent. Astăzi, votul nostru trebuie să fie direct pentru Moldova, cât și pentru Uniunea Europeană unită.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Moldau steht erneut an einem Wendepunkt. Die jüngsten politischen Entwicklungen in Chișinău zeigen, wie sensibel die innenpolitische Lage bleibt und wie entscheidend Stabilität, Reformfähigkeit und ein klarer europäischer Kurs jetzt sind.

Gerade vor diesem Hintergrund halte ich diesen Bericht für besonders wichtig. Er zeigt deutlich: Moldau hat trotz enormen äußeren Drucks bemerkenswerte Fortschritte gemacht im EU‑Beitrittsprozess – bei Reformen im Justiz- und Verwaltungsbereich und bei der wirtschaftlichen Annäherung an die Europäische Union.

Aber wir dürfen nicht naiv sein. Moldau steht unter einem anhaltenden hybriden Angriff – Desinformation, Cyberangriffe, Energie-Erpressung und russische Einflussnahme zielen darauf, den europäischen Kurs des Landes zu brechen.

Unsere Antwort muss klar sein: Wir unterstützen Moldau politisch, finanziell und sicherheitspolitisch. Die Beitrittsverhandlungen müssen auf Leistung beruhen, nicht auf Blockaden. Wer Reformen liefert, muss Fortschritt sehen. Moldaus europäische Zukunft ist nicht nur eine moldauische Frage, sie ist eine Frage der Glaubwürdigkeit und Sicherheit Europas.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Pani Komisarz! Mołdawia jest wyjątkowym krajem kandydatem. paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, the 2025 report on Moldova sends a clear message: despite an extremely challenging geopolitical and economic environment, Moldova continues to move forward on its European path.

The progress is concrete. Moldova is replacing its Soviet-era standards with European ones. These are not merely technical changes, but tangible steps, improving quality, safety and protection for Moldovan citizens. We also see progress in consumer protection. Moldova has made public services more accessible and effective.

Notably, Moldova has consistently cooperated on foreign policy issues, and aligns with the EU's common foreign and security policy positions. This is done in a very hostile environment, under significant internal and external challenges, such as persistent hostile Russian interference, as correctly noted in the report.

Of course, challenges remain and further work is needed, but today we should recognise the progress achieved. Moldova is making serious efforts, delivering concrete results and demonstrating through action its European ambitions.
These efforts deserve our recognition and our continued support, because we do not see them everywhere, and we value them when we see them.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, no entiendo en absoluto qué hacéis algunos diputados —casi todos españoles— aplaudiendo la ampliación de la Unión Europea antes en el debate anterior de Ucrania y ahora en el de Moldavia.

Que lo hagan los alemanes lo puedo entender, pero nosotros, los españoles, ¿no hemos leído aquí el estudio interno filtrado del propio Consejo de la Unión Europea en 2023, en el que se señala que España va a ser el único país que va a pasar de cobrar a pagar? ¿Saben ustedes lo que significan 3 000 millones de euros de la PAC menos para un agricultor en España, en Rumanía, en Portugal o en Italia?

¿Saben lo que significa meter al país más pobre de Europa, que es Moldavia, con 2,4 millones de habitantes —lo sé porque he estado en Moldavia como voluntario, con refugiados de Moldavia— y con una corrupción sistémica del 12 % del PIB? Hablamos de meter ahora mismo a un territorio que tiene 1 500 soldados rusos dentro, en Transnistria, con un referéndum europeo, por cierto, que sacó un 50,4 %, y gracias al voto de la diáspora, porque uno de cada tres moldavos viven fuera de su país.
En fin, entiendo que algunos sí, pero que los diputados españoles apoyen esto me parece surrealista.

interventions.speaker_label: Marta Kos, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable members of the European Parliament, it's really good to see that Moldova has so many supporters here in the European Parliament. Some of them are very passionate. Mr Andriukaitis, thank you for your passionate words. I am on your side. I would also like to see Members of the European Parliament from Moldova as soon as possible too.

Moldova has demonstrated determination and delivered meaningful reforms under exceptionally challenging circumstances. It deserves recognition for that progress and our continued support to move forward on its path to EU membership. We have organised the biggest investment conference to date at the beginning of June in Chişinău and the companies from the Member States are already coming. This is the only way to prosperity. So, they have to do the reforms, the investors will come, and then we can speak about the prosperity.

Regarding the question of when Moldova will be able to become a member of the EU: when all the reforms will be done, meaning Moldova has to deliver, but we have to deliver too. I have heard this today many times. So, it is also our responsibility that this will happen as soon as possible. I used to say that Moldova is the best student in my class. Since the last successful way on the reforms, I am saying that Moldova is the best performer in my class.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, first of all, I would like to thank all the shadow rapporteurs. It was really intellectually stimulating and a very constructive effort that produced this report. I think that all the pro-European groups who negotiated the report were brought together by a great sense of unity of purpose, but also a sense of urgency. I would also like to thank Commissioner Kos for her personal dedication and commitment to supporting, in every possible way, Moldova's very legitimate European aspirations. And I would like to thank all the colleagues for an extremely constructive debate here.

I hope that the report that we are going to be voting on tomorrow – and also tonight's debate – help us to send a very clear message to the Moldovan people and the Moldovan Government: a message of support and solidarity, but also a message of what our expectations are as to the next steps to be taken in this reform path.

I also hope that the report and the debates send a very clear message to our colleagues, the political leaders in our Member State capitals, who periodically meet around the Council table: a message that we expect them to live up to our end of the bargain, as I said, and to actually act with the same sense of urgency, because it is absolutely clear that the Russian pressure on Moldova will not dissipate until the successful completion of this process.

Moldova did not apply for membership and we did not launch this process in order for us to allow them to enjoy the process. It must be a purpose-driven process that will conclude in fully integrating Moldova into our European family without any unnecessary delay.

paragraphs.text: Poštovani predsjedavajući, povjerenice, kolegice i kolege, ovogodišnje izvješće odražava stvarnost u Srbiji u jednom od ključnih razdoblja njezine novije povijesti. Gotovo da nema poglavlja u kojem napredak prema članstvu u Europskoj uniji nije ocijenjen kao ograničen ili nepostojeći.

I naša se misija u Beogradu početkom godine odvijala u neobično teškim okolnostima. Zastupnici su bili izloženi verbalnim napadima predstavnika vlasti i provladinih medija, a visoki dužnosnici Srbije više su puta iznosili neutemeljene tvrdnje da Europska unija i neke njezine države članice potiču ili podržavaju tzv. obojenu revoluciju u Srbiji.

Uglavnom, napredak Srbije u ostvarivanju reformi važnima za napredak prema članstvu u Europskoj uniji značajno se usporio. U nekoliko ključnih područja, a posebno u vladavini prava, došlo je i do nazadovanja.

To se reflektira i preko ograničenog napretka u dijalogu Beograda i Prištine, kontinuiranog manjka usklađivanja sa zajedničkom vanjskom i sigurnosnom politikom, nedostatka istinske političke predanosti reformama, agresivne retorike prema Europskoj uniji, pogoršanja uvjeta za rad slobodnih medija i organizacija civilnog društva. Bilježi se kontinuirani neuspjeh u sveobuhvatnoj provedbi preporuka u izbornoj reformi jer i dalje postoji problem s regulatornim tijelom i s biračkim spiskom.

Dok vlasti u Srbiji i dalje predstavljaju članstvo u Europskoj uniji kao svoj strateški cilj, postupci njenog političkog vodstva često to ne potvrđuju. Zadnje izvješće Europske komisije također ukazuje na kontinuirano demokratsko nazadovanje, nedovoljan napredak u reformama vladavine prava i sve veći jaz između izrečenih europskih težnji Srbije i njezine političke prakse. Nažalost, ne vidimo ni napredak u istrazi o urušavanju nadstrešnice željezničkog kolodvora u Novom Sadu, što je potaknulo masovno nezadovoljstvo građana.

Zbog neispunjenih obveza ili ozbiljnog nedostatka rezultata, osobito u području vladavine prava, izvješće poziva Komisiju da zaustavi buduće isplate u okviru Instrumenta za reforme i rast za zapadni Balkan. Također se zalažem za reprogramiranje postojećih i budućih sredstava Europske unije kako bi se ojačala podrška reformi pravosuđa, naporima u borbi protiv korupcije, neovisnim medijima, organizacijama civilnog društva i neovisnom kulturnom sektoru.
Podsjetio bih kako je politika stabilokracije i gledanja kroz prste autokratima u posljednjih desetak godina stimulirala postojeće loše prilike na dobrom dijelu zapadnog Balkana.

Zato se ne moramo pitati kako bi danas prošao referendum o ulasku Srbije u Europsku uniju, upravo zbog niske podrške članstvu. Ima puno razloga zašto je ta podrška najniža u regiji, budući da se protueuropska retorika koristi godinama. Međutim, svakako je važan element za gubitak povjerenja u Europsku uniju i njezine institucije i toleriranje lažnog proeuropskog narativa vlasti u Beogradu svih proteklih godina.

Zbog toga sam uvjeren da je promašeno inzistiranje na otvaranju pregovaračkog klastera 3, čime bi se obnovili pregovori o pristupanju Srbije Europskoj uniji nakon četiri godine zastoja. Ta je stagnacija imala svoje jasne i opravdane razloge, baš kao što ih pokretanje nema ni danas.

Izvješće reflektira kontinuirano urušavanje demokratskih standarda u Srbiji. Zar treba nagraditi neusklađenost s europskom vanjskom politikom koja je tek na 63 posto, unatoč tome što druge države kandidatkinje nemaju problem potpunog usklađivanja? Uz jačanje veza s Kinom i Rusijom, imamo i slučaj da ministar u vladi ide u posjet Iranu, a nemojmo zaboraviti kako je predsjednica srpskog parlamenta svojedobno otišla i na inauguraciju Nicolasa Madura.

Osim toga, nemoguće je ne reagirati na pokušaje iz Beograda da se ugrozi održavanje samita Europske unije zapadnog Balkana nedavno u Crnoj Gori. Sve to pokazuje da odnosi Europske unije i Srbije ne mogu biti tek tako resetirani.

Izuzetno veliki problem je i stanje medija. Upravo se odvija proces preuzimanja i ono malo preostalih slobodnih medija koji lako mogu biti dovedeni u ovisnost od vlasti koja je dokazala da ne tolerira nikakvu kritiku.

Zato se ne moramo pitati kako bi danas prošao referendum o ulasku Srbije u Europsku uniju, upravo zbog niske podrške članstvu. Ima puno razloga zašto je ta podrška najniža u regiji, budući da se protueuropska retorika koristi godinama. Međutim, svakako je važan element za gubitak povjerenja u Europsku uniju i njezine institucije i toleriranje lažnog proeuropskog narativa vlasti u Beogradu svih proteklih godina.

Zbog toga sam uvjeren da je promašeno inzistiranje na otvaranju pregovaračkog klastera 3, čime bi se obnovili pregovori o pristupanju Srbije Europskoj uniji nakon četiri godine zastoja. Ta je stagnacija imala svoje jasne i opravdane razloge, baš kao što ih pokretanje nema ni danas.

Izvješće reflektira kontinuirano urušavanje demokratskih standarda u Srbiji. Zar treba nagraditi neusklađenost s europskom vanjskom politikom koja je tek na 63 posto, unatoč tome što druge države kandidatkinje nemaju problem potpunog usklađivanja? Uz jačanje veza s Kinom i Rusijom, imamo i slučaj da ministar u vladi ide u posjet Iranu, a nemojmo zaboraviti kako je predsjednica srpskog parlamenta svojedobno otišla i na inauguraciju Nicolasa Madura.

Osim toga, nemoguće je ne reagirati na pokušaje iz Beograda da se ugrozi održavanje samita Europske unije zapadnog Balkana nedavno u Crnoj Gori. Sve to pokazuje da odnosi Europske unije i Srbije ne mogu biti tek tako resetirani.

Izuzetno veliki problem je i stanje medija. Upravo se odvija proces preuzimanja i ono malo preostalih slobodnih medija koji lako mogu biti dovedeni u ovisnost od vlasti koja je dokazala da ne tolerira nikakvu kritiku.

interventions.speaker_label: Marta Kos, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, dear rapporteur Tonino Picula, thank you for your comprehensive report and for your work on Serbia. The Commission appreciates the opportunity for a separate debate on Serbia.

Serbia is an important partner in the region, with a clear EU-accession perspective. The European Commission therefore continues encouraging Serbia to seize the current opportunity to advance towards membership.

At the EU-Western Balkans Summit, we heard clear commitments from the Serbian leadership that the EU path is their strategic priority. We now need to see Serbia demonstrate its strategic commitments, address the EU's concerns and continue to deliver on the much-needed reforms.

As said many times, reforms on the rule of law, and respect for democratic principles and freedoms, will remain essential for Serbia's progress on its EU path. Two weeks ago, the Serbian Parliament took an important step in the right direction to correct the judicial laws adopted in January. This helps starting rebuilding the trust.

Serbia also made tangible progress in addressing key audit recommendations by revising legislation relevant for the electoral framework. In May, amendments to four election-related laws, among others, on the election of the Members of Parliament and on the election of the president, were adopted.
Two particularly important and substantial laws that concern the financing of political activities and the prevention of corruption are currently under preparation, meaning still to be done.

The recent invitation to OSCE/ODIHR to conduct the usual needs assessment mission is an important step to ensure, in a timely manner, a fully-fledged international election observation mission ahead of the next elections.

We now need to see Serbia advancing further on the electoral reform, in line with ODIHR recommendations, in a transparent and inclusive manner – strengthening media freedom and pluralism; ensuring respect for fundamental rights and freedoms, including freedom of peaceful assembly and academic freedom; and an enabling environment for civil society.
Recent developments on the formation of the so-called REM Council have been encouraging, and we hope that this regulatory body can start its important work soon. This is a long-awaited step.

Alignment with our EU objectives extends beyond internal policies to our common foreign and security policy. Serbia's European past therefore requires clear strategic choices. This also needs to be reflected in a consistent and high alignment with the Union's common foreign and security policy.

A credible European trajectory also means a commitment to regional stability, to normalisation of relations with Kosovo, and to a shared understanding of the security challenges facing our continent. It means tackling disinformation and abstaining from hostile political rhetoric, including against the EU, its institutions and honourable Members of this Parliament.

Serbia's commitment to the EU path and its political will to implement the required reforms also have to be strengthened via communication and concrete actions – including meaningful engagement on EU reforms – with the relevant stakeholders, including civil society organisations, to overcome the current deep divisions in Serbian society.

Dear honourable Members, with other countries advancing in the accession process, we do not want to see Serbia fall behind. This is why, in light of the recent – some positive – developments, the Commission renewed its recommendation to the Council to open Cluster 3 in the accession negotiations with Serbia.
The Commission will also continue to incentivise further reform progress for the benefit of all Serbian citizens and the whole Serbian society.

interventions.speaker_label: Davor Ivo Stier, on behalf of the PPE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the PPE Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, EU enlargement has regained its political importance. This is something that, in general, has benefited countries, but not in the case of Serbia. President Vučić made clear that Serbia can implement EU‑related reforms and has appointed a very professional negotiating operational team. But he also said that Serbia will not turn its back on Russia. Serbia does not perceive itself as part of the West, but pursues a non‑aligned policy, which is deeply rooted in society: it existed before Vučić and will probably continue after him.

While the EU should acknowledge this decision, Serbia needs to understand that it won't make progress towards EU membership if it keeps friendly relations with the EU's adversaries. Sometimes driven by a transactional logic, some key Member States have attempted to change Belgrade's policy. However, they have so far failed – sometimes increasing the level of frustration on all sides.

At the same time, Parliament's criticism, while honest and principled, has had little impact so far on changing the course of events. So what can be done? A realistic approach should envisage cooperation and partial and gradual integration in those areas of mutual benefit – from border management, trade, finance, energy and transport. A pragmatic but firm approach can bring results. We saw it with the repeal of the mortgage laws, with better cooperation on electoral reform, even with better cooperation with the Croatian National Council.

Of course, this should be continued and expanded to the benefit of both sides, but we should also be honest with each other: Serbia will not align with the EU any time soon. There is no political will for it, neither in the government nor in the opposition. To that situation, our response should not be appeasement or isolation, but rather a realistic engagement: firm on values and pragmatic on promoting our interests, without false promises about progress in the negotiations, but with a clear vision of a working relationship that serves the cause of peace in ...

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Andreas Schieder, on behalf of the S&D Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the S&D Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Madam Commissioner, I think it is important to say it again: we all want to see Serbia and especially the Serbian citizens in the European Union.

But there is one problem on this way, and the problem has a name. It's Aleksandar Vučić – because under his presidency, the country is going backwards – going backwards on democracy, on media freedom, on transparency, growing corruption is on the rise, the ministers attending the funeral in Iran. Also, Serbia and Belgrade sometimes is seen as a Moscow proxy. I think these are arguments enough also to discuss seriously to freeze further EU money.

Secondly, I think we have to express very clearly here from the European Parliament 100 % solidarity with the students movement. Every week, ten thousands are going on the street, risking a lot of their life, risking their studies and their future, but fighting for a better, a European future. And they have a simple demand, which is a clear, functioning, modern Serbian State. While they are not waving European flags, I think they expect that the European Union is supporting these students' demands: to have a modern, functional, clean Serbian State.

The last point: Vučić now called for new elections. Nobody knows exactly when. It seems to be another trick of this magician of debate. But we have to say, before it comes to election, we need an electoral law which is fulfilling the need for clear and fair elections. We need that the OSCE or the European Parliament recommendations are implemented, and also we need a clear and fair voter registration process. Otherwise, the elections will result in the same result like the old elections.

interventions.speaker_label: Annamária Vicsek, a PfE képviselőcsoport nevében.

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Úr! Mindnyájan egyetérthetünk abban, hogy Szerbia előtt ma komoly kihívások állnak. Folytatni kell a reformokat, erősíteni kell a társadalmi párbeszédet, és előre kell vinni az európai integrációs folyamatot. Ugyanakkor fontos, hogy a mai vitát a jelenlegi európai politikai környezetben értelmezzük. Az elmúlt hetekben világos üzenetet kaptunk: az Európai Unió stratégiai prioritásként tekint a bővítésre. Montenegró újabb tárgyalási fejezeteket zár le. Ukrajna és Moldova megnyitotta első tárgyalási klaszterét. Tegnap az Európai Bizottság egyértelművé tette, hogy támogatja a harmadik tárgyalási klaszter júliusi megnyitását Szerbia számára, mert megítélése szerint ennek feltételei teljesültek. Ez egy kedvező politikai pillanat, amelyet sem Szerbiának, sem az Európai Uniónak nem szabad elszalasztania.

A hiányosságokat meg kell nevezni, de ugyanolyan fontos elismerni azokat az eredményeket is, amelyek megszülettek. Az elmúlt hónapokban Szerbia 23 kulcsfontosságú törvényt fogadott el, köztük uniós jogharmonizációs, igazságügyi és választási reformokat. A szerb parlament ezen a héten további, az ODIR ajánlásait, valamint a 23/24-es tárgyalási fejezetet érintő jogszabályokat tárgyal. Májusban a kormány elfogadta a kisebbségi cselekvési tervet is. Sajnálatos módon a jelentés hangvétele nem tükrözi ezt a kiegyensúlyozott megközelítést. Szinte kizárólag a hiányosságokra összpontosít, miközben a reformok és az elért eredmények csak elvétve jelennek meg benne.

Ha meg is jelenik benne dicséret, újabb bírálatok relativizálják az elismerést. A hiteles és érdemalapú bővítési politika nem csak a hiányosságok feltárását, hanem a reformok eredményeinek elismerését is megköveteli. Csak így őrizhetjük meg a bővítési politika hitelességét, ami Szerbia, a Nyugat-Balkán és az Európai Unió közös érdekét szolgálja.

interventions.speaker_label: Şerban Dimitrie Sturdza, în numele grupului ECR.

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, doamnă comisar, stimați colegi, aderarea Serbiei la Uniunea Europeană trebuie să însemne reforme reale, stat de drept și respect deplin pentru minoritățile naționale. Este necesar ca Serbia să trateze drepturile românilor de pe teritoriul său cu seriozitate, fără atribuirea de identități artificiale precum vlahi. Românii sunt români, oriunde ar fi.

Totodată, trebuie să vedem relații de bună vecinătate prin fapte și aici mă refer la proiectul Porților de Fier III de pe Dunăre, pentru că vorbim despre un fluviu internațional, nu despre proprietatea exclusivă a unui stat. De aceea, orice proiect major care poate afecta regimul apelor, securitatea energetică, echilibrul ecologic sau agricultura trebuie discutat transparent cu vecinii, înainte de a deveni o problemă politică.
Integrarea europeană înseamnă încredere, iar încrederea se construiește prin transparență, cooperare și respect reciproc.

interventions.speaker_label: Helmut Brandstätter, on behalf of the Renew Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Renew Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear Commissioner, I admire the young Serbian people. They are very brave; they go on the street; they fight for a life in freedom. And then they listen to the Commission, and the Commission says, 'we want to open Cluster 3, we want to continue the process'. No! Right now it's not the moment to continue the process because there is a backlash.

There are no reforms, as I hear now. On the contrary, what does Mr Vučić say? He cannot leave power. He takes Putin as a role model. He says: 'what's fine for Putin is now fine for me, so I want to be again the Prime Minister and not the President'. Here, you see, it's not about democracy; it's not about freedom. But it's our job to say to the Serbian people: 'we are on your side'. The Serbians are Europeans like us; the Serbians should be members of the European Union. But autocracy has no place here.

So I think, yes, Commissioner, you said there should be observation of the elections, but there also should be more than only observation during the elections. We need a long observation. We need contact with the opposition, which is also here, with the students. Serbia: yes! Autocracy: no!

paragraphs.text: Gospod predsednik, spoštovani! Evropski parlament ni sovražnik srbskega naroda. Prav tako Evropski parlament ni ovira Srbije na poti k Evropski uniji. Je pa Evropski parlament neomajni podpornik demokracije ter vseh tistih, ki se zanjo borijo.
Svoboda medijev, svoboda izražanja, vladavina prava, spoštovanje drugače mislečih in boj proti korupciji žal nimajo domovinske pravice v Srbiji.

interventions.speaker_label: Jonas Sjöstedt, för The Left gruppen.

paragraphs.text: Herr talman! Serbien står inför ett verkligt vägskäl. På ena sidan Vučićs auktoritära högerregering som aktivt förtrycker oppositionen – ett styre i grunden präglat av korruption och maktmissbruk. Vi ser hur rättsstaten undergrävs. Vi ser hur medias frihet inskränks.

På den andra sidan finns en av Europas mest dynamiska, intressanta och välorganiserade demokratirörelser. De serbiska studenterna har skapat någonting unikt, en gräsrotsrörelse, demokratisk från grunden, som utmanar makten genom ständiga nytänkande, demokratiska protester. De bär fröet till en bättre framtid för Serbien.

Vår uppgift är väldigt tydlig: Det är att göra allt vi kan för ett rättvist val. När det gäller vallagen, när det gäller registreringen av väljare och inte minst när det gäller genomförandet. Det är vårt ansvar.

interventions.text:
Herr talman! Serbien står inför ett verkligt vägskäl. På ena sidan Vučićs auktoritära högerregering som aktivt förtrycker oppositionen – ett styre i grunden präglat av korruption och maktmissbruk. Vi ser hur rättsstaten undergrävs. Vi ser hur medias frihet inskränks.

På den andra sidan finns en av Europas mest dynamiska, intressanta och välorganiserade demokratirörelser. De serbiska studenterna har skapat någonting unikt, en gräsrotsrörelse, demokratisk från grunden, som utmanar makten genom ständiga nytänkande, demokratiska protester. De bär fröet till en bättre framtid för Serbien.

Vår uppgift är väldigt tydlig: Det är att göra allt vi kan för ett rättvist val. När det gäller vallagen, när det gäller registreringen av väljare och inte minst när det gäller genomförandet. Det är vårt ansvar.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Gestern hat Lars Klingbeil in Berlin den Bundeshaushalt für 2027 vorgestellt: 200 Milliarden Euro neue Schulden; der deutsche Staat ist nur noch auf Pump finanzierbar. Während Deutschland pleite geht, wollen Sie hier immer mehr Mitglieder in die Europäische Union aufnehmen. Die Konrad‑Adenauer‑Stiftung der CDU schätzt, dass der Beitritt Serbiens 3 Milliarden Euro kosten wird, der gesamte Westbalkan 7 Milliarden Euro im Jahr. Deutsche Steuerzahler werden ein Viertel der Kosten schultern müssen, also etwa 2 Milliarden Euro – das ist ungefähr der Betrag, den die Bundesregierung bei pflegenden Angehörigen einsparen möchte. Mit anderen Worten: Deutsche, die ihre Eltern pflegen, bekommen die Rente gekürzt, damit CDU und SPD ihre Steuergelder auf dem Balkan verjubeln können. Ich wundere mich, dass es überhaupt noch Wähler gibt, die diesen Parteien ihre Stimmen geben.

Seit zwei Jahren gehen die Serben jetzt auf die Straße wegen der Korruption in ihrem Land. Der serbische Präsident hat deshalb seinen Rücktritt erklärt, weil er im Unterschied zu deutschen Politikern bereit ist, Verantwortung für die Fehler seiner Regierung zu übernehmen. Ich finde das vorbildlich; Ursula von der Leyen oder Friedrich Merz sollten sich daran ein Beispiel nehmen und es ihm gleichtun.
Wir wollen eine privilegierte Partnerschaft mit Belgrad. Bevor wir aber mit deutschen Steuergeldern den Balkan sanieren, müssen wir erst einmal Deutschland wieder aufbauen.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Mr Brandstätter, dear Helmut, indeed, the election observation is not enough. That's why, for any new elections, we expect them to take place under conditions which ensure free and fair elections, in accordance with the European and international standards.

So the electoral process requires further tangible improvement and reforms. For this, Serbia should build on the first positive steps taken to address concerns about the integrity of the electoral register and the electoral legislation. But work still needs to be done.
So progress on Serbia's path is in the interest of the EU, and when we speak about supporting Serbia, we speak about supporting Serbian citizens.

paragraphs.text: Poštovani predsjedavajući, naravno, zahvaljujem svima na doprinosu u večerašnjoj raspravi, a pogotovo kolegama izvjestiteljima iz sjene na odličnoj suradnji.

Vjerujem da su današnju raspravu pratili ne samo građani Europske unije, već, prije svega, i građani Srbije. Vjerujem i da građani Srbije žele slobodne i poštene izbore i priliku da grade bolju europsku budućnost, ali nakon godina demokratskog nazadovanja Europska unija ne smije nagraditi srpsku vlast napretkom na pristupnom putu na temelju kvazi reformi.

Srbija je najveća zemlja na zapadnom Balkanu s najvećim kapacitetom za napredak na putu prema članstvu u Europsku uniju. Međutim, umjesto otvaranja i zatvaranja pregovaračkih poglavlja, srpska vlada samo otvara nove dileme i nove napetosti prema susjedima.

Ne možemo govoriti o napretku u dijalogu s Kosovom ako se ne privedu odgovorni za teroristički napad u Banjskoj. Ne možemo govoriti o iskoraku u vladavini prava ako se pokušava ispravljati nešto što je prvobitno urađeno potpuno pogrešno jer ti Mrdićevi zakoni, zapravo Vučićevi zakoni, nisu ni trebali biti usvojeni.

Mi kao Europski parlament moramo biti čvrsti u svojoj predanosti poštivanju vrijednosti i pravila. Ne možemo odšutjeti nazadovanje u vladavini prava, eroziji demokratskih standarda i destruktivnom utjecaju na stabilnost regije.

Ako vlasti u Srbiji žele napredovati na svom putu prema Europskoj uniji, moraju donijeti jasan strateški izbor, napraviti ključne reforme te se u potpunosti uskladiti s vanjskom sigurnosnom politikom Europske unije i sankcijama Europske unije prema Rusiji.

paragraphs.text: Kinga Gál (PfE), írásbanAz Európai Parlament Szerbiáról szóló éves jelentése minden korábbinál kritikusabb és elfogultabb.A jelentés semmilyen reformtevékenységet és eddigi eredményt nem ismer el és egyoldalú, politikailag motivált megközelítést alkalmaz. Ez a hozzáállás az Unió részéről sajnos egyre jellemzőbb a nyugat-balkáni országok és különösen Szerbia esetében, ez pedig lépten-nyomon gyengíti az Európai Unió hitelességét a térségben.Ez a tendencia azért is aggasztó, mert Szerbia kulcsország a Nyugat-Balkán stabilitása szempontjából, az Uniónak pedig kiegyensúlyozott, felelős és partneri megközelítésre lenne szüksége. A közös cél a térség stabilitásának megőrzése, amelyhez csak egy hiteles, objektív és az eredményeket is elismerő uniós hozzáállás vezethet.A most tárgyalt jelentés patrióta felelőseként a szöveget kiegyensúlyozatlannak látom. Kétségtelen, hogy számos területen van még mit teljesítenie az országnak, de értékelni kellene a szerb kormány európai elköteleződését és eddig tett erőfeszítéseit az energiapolitika, a családpolitika, a vízumpolitika és a kisebbségpolitika területén. A szöveg ehelyett a hiányosságok bemutatására koncentrál és súlyosan igazságtalan ideológiai torzításokat tartalmaz. A bővítéspolitikában nincs helye kettős mércének, mégis az aktuálpolitikai érdek egyre hangsúlyosabbá válik a semleges, teljesítményen alapuló elbírálás helyett.Szerbia európai integrációja hozzájárulhat az illegális migráció megfékezéséhez és az energiaellátás hosszú távú biztosításához. Európa és így Magyarország érdeke is egy stabil, az Unió felé elkötelezett Szerbia.

paragraphs.text: Κύριε Πρόεδρε, ο κανονισμός που ψηφίστηκε επικαλείται τα δικαιώματα των επιβατών στις αεροπορικές μεταφορές, ενώ ικανοποιεί όλες τις απαιτήσεις των μεγάλων ομίλων του κλάδου που σημειώνουν κέρδη ρεκόρ και έχουν ήδη μπουκώσει από κρατικές και ευρωενωσιακές επιδοτήσεις. Μειώνει περαιτέρω τις υποχρεώσεις των αεροπορικών εταιρειών, ψαλιδίζει τις αποζημιώσεις για τους επιβάτες και ανοίγει τον δρόμο για οριστικό περιορισμό τους, διατηρώντας την έννοια-λάστιχο των έκτακτων περιστάσεων, που δίνει την ικανότητα στους ομίλους να αποφεύγουν αποζημιώσεις κατά το δοκούν και να θησαυρίζουν ακόμα και από τις χειραποσκευές στην καμπίνα, όπως και από τις διαστάσεις της βαλίτσας.

Την ίδια στιγμή, οι εταιρείες, στη βάση της απελευθερωμένης αγοράς, έχουν εκτοξεύσει τις τιμές και εκμηδενίσει τις όποιες υπηρεσίες στους επιβάτες. Κριτήριο δράσης τους είναι το κέρδος, όπως βεβαίως και των κυβερνήσεων και της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης, που καταδικάζουν τις υπηρεσίες πολιτικής αεροπορίας να λειτουργούν με απαρχαιωμένες υποδομές και λιγοστό προσωπικό σε καθεστώς εντατικοποίησης, βάζοντας σε κίνδυνο την ασφάλεια των πτήσεων. Δεν υπάρχει άλλος δρόμος: Για να κερδίσει δικαιώματα και ασφάλεια ο λαός, πρέπει να χάσει το κεφάλαιο.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, en este pleno de julio del Parlamento Europeo ha tenido lugar la votación definitiva del Reglamento sobre los derechos de los pasajeros aéreos y es una votación que tiene dos rasgos extraordinarios que merecen subrayarse.

El primero es la amplísima mayoría: ha votado favorablemente el arco parlamentario casi entero. Ha recibido votos favorables de todos los grupos parlamentarios. La razón es sencilla: después de trece años de bloqueo, por fin se ha llegado a un acuerdo con el Consejo.

El segundo rasgo extraordinario es que, por fin, se produce un avance en los derechos de la ciudadanía y, particularmente, de los pasajeros y muchas veces los derechos laborales —incluso los derechos fundamentales en la Unión Europea— han venido de la mano de los derechos de los consumidores.

Por fin hay un derecho de compensación frente a los abusos de las compañías aéreas, los retrasos, los sobreprecios y las sobreventas, por fin el derecho reconocido a embarcar la maleta en cabina y por fin facilidades expresas para las personas con dificultades de movilidad, para que puedan ejercer sus derechos en igualdad de condiciones con respecto de todos los demás.

El segundo rasgo extraordinario es que, por fin, se produce un avance en los derechos de la ciudadanía y, particularmente, de los pasajeros y muchas veces los derechos laborales —incluso los derechos fundamentales en la Unión Europea— han venido de la mano de los derechos de los consumidores.

Por fin hay un derecho de compensación frente a los abusos de las compañías aéreas, los retrasos, los sobreprecios y las sobreventas, por fin el derecho reconocido a embarcar la maleta en cabina y por fin facilidades expresas para las personas con dificultades de movilidad, para que puedan ejercer sus derechos en igualdad de condiciones con respecto de todos los demás.

paragraphs.text: Κύριε Πρόεδρε, ο κανονισμός υπηρετεί τις ανάγκες του κεφαλαίου για φθηνότερη και πιο ευέλικτη εργατική δύναμη. Στην πράξη, προσαρμόζει το ισχύον πλαίσιο εξατομικευμένης και εμπορευματοποιημένης ασφάλισης πείνας, με γενίκευση των επαγγελματικών ταμείων στις ανάγκες της αγοράς, όπως προανήγγειλε πρόσφατα η κυβέρνηση της Νέας Δημοκρατίας μέσω της Τράπεζας της Ελλάδας. Επιδίωξή του η διασυνοριακή κινητικότητα, δηλαδή η μαζική μετανάστευση από χώρα σε χώρα, κυνηγώντας ένα μεροκάματο.

Στην Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση της πολεμικής οικονομίας και εμπλοκής, όπου ο ένας στους τρεις εργαζόμενους είναι και επίσημα φτωχός και η ανεργία θερίζει, ο κανονισμός προτείνει πιο αυστηρούς όρους πρόσβασης στο επίδομα ανεργίας και διατήρησής του. Στόχος του κανονισμού είναι το ξήλωμα των εργατικών δικαιωμάτων, τα βάρη κράτους/ εργοδοσίας να μετατραπούν σε απώλειες για τους εργαζόμενους.

Για να κερδίσουν οι εργαζόμενοι, πρέπει να χάσει το κεφάλαιο, τα κόμματα που το υπηρετούν και οι διεθνείς του συμμαχίες. Να οργανώσουν τώρα την πάλη τους για συλλογικές συμβάσεις εργασίας με αξιοπρεπείς μισθούς, με πλήρη ασφαλιστικά δικαιώματα και μείωση του εργάσιμου χρόνου.
